newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi homes with mosquitoes face prosecution.
newsitem.headline: Delhi homes with mosquitoes face prosecution.

text.p: The Indian government on Wednesday instructed authorities in the capital to prosecute house owners who failed to eradicate mosquitoes which have caused a deadly outbreak of dengue fever.
It said in a statement that a meeting of health experts from the federal government, the city of Delhi and the Indian Red Cross Society had reviewed measures to combat the outbreak.
Delhi municipal authorities had been told "to launch vigorous prosecution against those who have failed to prevent mosquito breeding within their houses," the statement said.
Domestic news agencies said 177 people have died in the disease. More than 350 fresh cases were reported on Wednesday.
Authorities had surveyed 1.35 million households and found mosquitoes breeding in more than 55,000 of them, it said.

Mosquitoes carry the virus which causes dengue, also called breakbone fever. The disease erupted in the Indian capital in the last week of August during annual monsoon rains, and more than 4,000 victims have been brought or admitted to local hospitals.
Earlier this week authorities called in the army to spray insecticides in mosquito-infested areas and open its hospitals to dengue patients.
The government statement said adequate amounts of blood platelets and blood plasma were available for both government and private hospitals.
Delhi authorities had eight to 10 days' worth of Pyrethrum insecticide, and more was on the way, it said.
